annotation.title_clean: Technology at Work v2.0: The Future Is Not What It Used to Be
annotation.title_en: Technology at Work v2.0: The Future Is Not What It Used to Be
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Frey, C.B.; Osborne, M.A.; Holmes, C.; Rahbari, E.; Curmi, E.; et al.
annotation.venue: Citi GPS: Global Perspectives & Solutions (Citi and Oxford Martin School)
annotation.summary_en: Citi GPS and Oxford Martin School report on automation's labour-market effects: jobs at risk across countries and cities, new job creation, productivity, inflation, and policy responses including education. It includes a section on robot laws covering privacy, ethics and liability. The URL title suggests a different article, but the content is this report.
key_provisions_or_claims: Extends the finding that 47% of US jobs are at risk to other countries and cities.
Perception/manipulation, creativity and social intelligence are the main bottlenecks to automation.
Recommends investment in education and skills and support for technological dynamism and job creation in cities.
Considers whether robot laws on privacy, ethics and liability will slow adoption.
Questions whether traditional measures capture productivity and GDP gains from automation.
